predecessors.note: The Irish Free State dossier (eu-21-e) ends on 29 December 1937 with Éire as its successor; the Constitution of Ireland 'replaced the Constitution of the Irish Free State'.

keyframe_review.note: 74,947 km2 for 1938-1972 against the infobox's 70,273 km2 (ratio 1.07): the Republic without Northern Ireland, with a coarser coastline. The shape includes the three Treaty Ports, which the UK handed back in July to October 1938 (ledger). Valid 1938-1972.
74,990 km2: the same island share, 43 km2 larger than the other shapes, an outline difference with no event (the state 'joined the EC as a member state on 1 January 1973'). Valid 1973-1975.

region.text: the twenty-six counties that form the state, the island of Ireland without Northern Ireland

ledger.note: 29 December 1937: the Constitution of Ireland creates Éire. 'The constitution came into force on 29 December 1937'; it 'replaced the Constitution of the Irish Free State' and Article 4 says 'the name of the State is Éire, or, in the English language, Ireland' (the Éire page). The plebiscite was on 1 July 1937. Articles 2 and 3 described 'the whole island of Ireland' as the national territory, a claim withdrawn in 1999; it gives no land.

region.text: Spike Island and its fortifications off Cobh (Queenstown), Cork Harbour

ledger.note: 29 December 1937: the state is born with three ports still British. The UK kept 'Berehaven, Spike Island (off modern Cobh, formerly Queenstown), and Lough Swilly' under the Treaty signed on 6 December 1921; they were handed over in 1938 (this event: Spike Island).

region.text: the Berehaven forts, Bere Island and Castletownbere

ledger.note: 29 December 1937: the Berehaven forts are still British ('The Berehaven forts were handed over' only on 29 September 1938).

region.text: the Lough Swilly forts at Dunree and Leenan

ledger.note: 29 December 1937: the Lough Swilly forts at Dunree and Leenan are still British. The page does not name Buncrana; the town is the place the forts lie by.

region.text: Spike Island and its fortifications off Cobh (Queenstown), Cork Harbour

ledger.note: 11 July 1938: Spike Island is handed back. 'British troops handed custody of the island and its fortifications to Irish troops at Cobh' after the Anglo-Irish Trade Agreement of 25 April 1938.

region.text: the Berehaven forts, Bere Island and Castletownbere

ledger.note: 29 September 1938: the Berehaven forts are handed back. The Times of 1 October 1938: 'The last of the British troops stationed at the Southern Irish coast defences left last night for England.'

region.text: the Lough Swilly forts at Dunree and Leenan

ledger.note: 3 October 1938: the Lough Swilly forts at Dunree and Leenan are surrendered to Irish forces, the last of the Treaty Ports; the Agreement had set 31 December 1938 as the latest date.

18 April 1949: the state becomes the Republic of Ireland. The Republic of Ireland Act 1948, signed on 21 December 1948, 'came into force on 18 April 1949, Easter Monday'; it repealed the External Relations Act 1936 and the state left the Commonwealth. The Éire page: the Ireland Act 1949 changed 'the English-law name of the state' to 'Republic of Ireland'. Same state, same land, same colour.

certainty.note: The state is the twenty-six counties and shares its only land border with Northern Ireland; the Constitution's claim to the whole island (Articles 2 and 3, 1937) was removed in 1999 and never moved the border. The Treaty Port enclaves were British until 1938.

notes:
Page budget (up to 5) spent on Éire, Constitution of Ireland, Treaty Ports (Ireland), Republic of Ireland Act 1948 and Republic of Ireland.

One state, three names: the Irish Free State (separate dossier, to 29 December 1937), Éire (this dossier from 29 December 1937) and the Republic of Ireland (a rename from 18 April 1949, no territorial change). Cliopatria's row 'Éire' runs 1938-2024 and no shape changes; the 1973-1975 shape is 43 km2 larger than the others (outline noise).

Counterpart: 'united-kingdom' is the slug eu-11 is to give the UK from 1801 (Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Great Britain' row runs to 2024); it has no dossier yet. The Treaty Ports pair (three starts, three ends, one counterpart) lets the map hatch the three enclaves until their handovers; each is one or two H3 cells and may not show at the grid's scale.

Not settled: the 1937 claim to Northern Ireland (Articles 2 and 3) is a claim, not an event, and is recorded only in the found event and certainty; the Ireland Act 1949 (UK) and Northern Ireland's status are not dated on the pages opened. The Emergency (neutrality, 1939-1945) is not a war of this state and has no entry. No Anglo-Irish Trade War, Border Campaign or Troubles page was opened, so no event is recorded for them; none moved a border.
Gazetteer names needed: Cobh, Castletownbere (Berehaven), Buncrana (Lough Swilly); the validator's resolve check lists them.
